concepts.name: Second-order linear differential equation
concepts.statement: A second-order differential equation is linear if it can be written in the form a₂(x)y″ + a₁(x)y′ + a₀(x)y = r(x), where a₂(x), a₁(x), a₀(x) and r(x) are real-valued functions and a₂(x) is not identically zero; y and its derivatives are raised only to the first power and are not multiplied by one another.

concepts.name: Homogeneous linear equation
concepts.statement: A second-order linear differential equation a₂(x)y″ + a₁(x)y′ + a₀(x)y = r(x) is a homogeneous linear equation if r(x) = 0 for every value of x: every term contains y or one of its derivatives.

concepts.name: Nonhomogeneous linear equation
concepts.statement: A second-order linear differential equation a₂(x)y″ + a₁(x)y′ + a₀(x)y = r(x) is a nonhomogeneous linear equation if r(x) ≠ 0 for some value of x.

concepts.name: Superposition principle
concepts.statement: If y₁(x) and y₂(x) are solutions to a linear homogeneous differential equation, then the function y(x) = c₁y₁(x) + c₂y₂(x), where c₁ and c₂ are constants, is also a solution.

concepts.name: Linear independence
concepts.statement: A set of functions f₁(x), f₂(x), …, fₙ(x) is linearly dependent if there are constants c₁, c₂, …, cₙ, not all zero, such that c₁f₁(x) + c₂f₂(x) + ⋯ + cₙfₙ(x) = 0 for all x over the interval of interest; a set of functions that is not linearly dependent is linearly independent.

concepts.name: Linear dependence of two functions
concepts.statement: Two functions f₁(x) and f₂(x) are linearly dependent if either one of them is identically zero or if f₁(x) = Cf₂(x) for some constant C and for all x over the interval of interest; functions that are not linearly dependent are linearly independent.

concepts.name: General solution to a homogeneous equation
concepts.statement: If y₁(x) and y₂(x) are linearly independent solutions to a second-order, linear, homogeneous differential equation, then the general solution is given by y(x) = c₁y₁(x) + c₂y₂(x), where c₁ and c₂ are constants: every expression of that form is a solution, and every solution can be written in that form.

concepts.name: Second-order equation with constant coefficients
concepts.statement: A second-order linear homogeneous differential equation with constant coefficients has the form ay″ + by′ + cy = 0, where a, b and c are constants.

concepts.name: Characteristic equation
concepts.statement: The characteristic equation of the differential equation ay″ + by′ + cy = 0 is aλ² + bλ + c = 0; y(x) = e^{λx} is a solution exactly when λ is a root of it, and the roots are found by factoring or by the quadratic formula λ = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a).

concepts.name: Solution for distinct real roots
concepts.statement: If the characteristic equation has distinct real roots λ₁ and λ₂, then e^{λ₁x} and e^{λ₂x} are linearly independent solutions to ay″ + by′ + cy = 0, and the general solution is y(x) = c₁e^{λ₁x} + c₂e^{λ₂x}.

concepts.name: Solution for a repeated real root
concepts.statement: If the characteristic equation has a repeated real root λ, then b² − 4ac = 0, e^{λx} and xe^{λx} are linearly independent solutions, and the general solution to ay″ + by′ + cy = 0 is y(x) = c₁e^{λx} + c₂xe^{λx}.

concepts.name: Euler’s formula
concepts.statement: Euler’s formula expresses an exponential function with an imaginary exponent through sines and cosines: e^{iθ} = cos θ + i sin θ for all real numbers θ.

concepts.name: Solution for complex conjugate roots
concepts.statement: If b² − 4ac < 0, the characteristic equation has complex conjugate roots α ± βi, and the general solution to ay″ + by′ + cy = 0 is y(x) = e^{αx}(c₁ cos βx + c₂ sin βx), built from the two linearly independent real-value solutions e^{αx} cos βx and e^{αx} sin βx.

concepts.name: Solving with the characteristic equation
concepts.statement: To solve a second-order differential equation with constant coefficients: write it in the form ay″ + by′ + cy = 0; find the corresponding characteristic equation aλ² + bλ + c = 0; factor it or use the quadratic formula to find the roots; and write the general solution by whether the roots are distinct and real, a single repeated real root, or complex conjugates.

concepts.name: Boundary conditions
concepts.statement: Boundary conditions give the state of a system at two different times, such as y(t₀) = y₀ and y(t₁) = y₁ for the position of a spring-mass system.

concepts.name: Boundary-value problem
concepts.statement: A boundary-value problem is a differential equation with associated boundary conditions; solving it means finding the solution of the differential equation that satisfies the boundary conditions.

concepts.name: Uniqueness of solutions to initial-value and boundary-value problems
concepts.statement: For constant-coefficient, second-order equations, an initial-value problem with two initial conditions is guaranteed to have a unique solution, while a boundary-value problem with two boundary conditions may have a unique solution, many solutions, or no solution at all.

concepts.name: Complementary equation
concepts.statement: For the nonhomogeneous linear differential equation a₂(x)y″ + a₁(x)y′ + a₀(x)y = r(x), the associated homogeneous equation a₂(x)y″ + a₁(x)y′ + a₀(x)y = 0 is called the complementary equation.

concepts.name: General solution to a nonhomogeneous equation
concepts.statement: Let y_p(x) be any particular solution to the nonhomogeneous linear differential equation a₂(x)y″ + a₁(x)y′ + a₀(x)y = r(x), and let c₁y₁(x) + c₂y₂(x) denote the general solution to the complementary equation. Then the general solution to the nonhomogeneous equation is y(x) = c₁y₁(x) + c₂y₂(x) + y_p(x).

concepts.name: Method of undetermined coefficients
concepts.statement: The method of undetermined coefficients finds a particular solution of ay″ + by′ + cy = r(x) when r(x) is a combination of polynomials, exponentials, sines and cosines: solve the complementary equation; guess y_p(x) of the same form as r(x), with every lower-order term; multiply the guess by x until no term of it solves the complementary equation; substitute it into the equation and equate like terms to find its coefficients; and add it to the general solution of the complementary equation.

concepts.name: Cramer’s rule
concepts.statement: The system a₁z₁ + b₁z₂ = r₁, a₂z₁ + b₂z₂ = r₂ has a unique solution if and only if the determinant of the coefficients is not zero; then z₁ and z₂ are the quotients of the determinants with the r column in place of the z₁ or z₂ column by the determinant of the coefficients.

concepts.name: Method of variation of parameters
concepts.statement: The method of variation of parameters finds a particular solution of y″ + py′ + qy = r(x) for any r(x): solve the complementary equation for c₁y₁(x) + c₂y₂(x); find u′(x) and v′(x) with u′y₁ + v′y₂ = 0 and u′y₁′ + v′y₂′ = r(x), by Cramer’s rule or another technique; integrate to find u(x) and v(x), so that y_p(x) = u(x)y₁(x) + v(x)y₂(x); and add y_p to the general solution of the complementary equation.

concepts.name: Simple harmonic motion
concepts.statement: A mass m on a spring with spring constant k, displaced x(t) from equilibrium with down positive, satisfies mx″ + kx = 0 by Hooke’s law and Newton’s second law, or x″ + ω²x = 0 with the angular frequency ω = √(k/m); its general solution x(t) = c₁ cos ωt + c₂ sin ωt is simple harmonic motion, with period T = 2π/ω and frequency f = 1/T = ω/2π.

concepts.name: Solution to the equation for simple harmonic motion
concepts.statement: The function x(t) = c₁ cos(ωt) + c₂ sin(ωt) can be written in the form x(t) = A sin(ωt + ϕ), where the amplitude is A = √(c₁² + c₂²) and the phase shift ϕ satisfies tan ϕ = c₁/c₂, with ϕ taken in the quadrant the signs of c₁ and c₂ give.

concepts.name: Damped spring-mass system
concepts.statement: With a damping force −bx′ proportional to the velocity, for some constant b > 0, a spring-mass system satisfies mx″ + bx′ + kx = 0, whose characteristic equation mλ² + bλ + k = 0 has roots λ = (−b ± √(b² − 4mk))/(2m); for every damped system, lim_{t→∞} x(t) = 0.

concepts.name: Overdamped system
concepts.statement: A damped spring-mass system is overdamped when b² > 4mk: the general solution x(t) = c₁e^{λ₁t} + c₂e^{λ₂t} has λ₁ and λ₂ both less than zero, and the mass moves back toward equilibrium with no more than one change of direction, without oscillating.

concepts.name: Critically damped system
concepts.statement: A damped spring-mass system is critically damped when b² = 4mk: the general solution x(t) = c₁e^{λ₁t} + c₂te^{λ₁t} has λ₁ less than zero; the mass does not oscillate, but any slight reduction in the damping would make it oscillate.

concepts.name: Underdamped system
concepts.statement: A damped spring-mass system is underdamped when b² < 4mk: the general solution x(t) = e^{αt}(c₁ cos(βt) + c₂ sin(βt)) has α less than zero, so the mass oscillates while the amplitude of its oscillations decreases over time.

concepts.name: Forced vibrations
concepts.statement: A spring-mass system acted on by an external force f(t) satisfies the nonhomogeneous equation mx″ + bx′ + kx = f(t), whose solutions have the form x(t) = c₁x₁(t) + c₂x₂(t) + x_p(t): the general solution to the complementary equation plus a particular solution.

concepts.name: Transient solution
concepts.statement: In a damped forced system, the part c₁x₁(t) + c₂x₂(t) of the solution that solves the complementary equation tends to zero as t → ∞ and does not affect the long-term behavior of the system; it is called the transient solution.

concepts.name: Steady-state solution
concepts.statement: The steady-state solution of a nonhomogeneous differential equation is the particular solution x_p(t), which determines the long-term behavior of the system once the transient solution has died away.

concepts.name: Resonance
concepts.statement: The frequency f = ω/2π of an undamped system is its natural frequency; if an external force acting on the system has a frequency close to the natural frequency, resonance results: the external force reinforces and amplifies the natural motion of the system.

concepts.name: RLC series circuit
concepts.statement: In an RLC series circuit with inductance L, resistance R, capacitance C and voltage source E(t), the voltage drops E_L = L dI/dt, E_R = RI and E_C = q/C sum to E(t) by Kirchhoff’s voltage rule; with I = dq/dt the charge q(t) on the capacitor satisfies L d²q/dt² + R dq/dt + q/C = E(t), an equation analogous to that of a spring-mass system.

concepts.name: Bessel equation
concepts.statement: The Bessel equation of order n is x²y″ + xy′ + (x² − n²)y = 0; it arises in physical applications involving cylindrical coordinates, such as the vibration of a circular drum head and the transient heating or cooling of a cylinder, and its solutions are Bessel functions.

concepts.name: Series solution of the Bessel equation of order 0
concepts.statement: A power series solution to the Bessel equation of order 0, x²y″ + xy′ + x²y = 0, is y(x) = a₀ Σ_{k=0}^{∞} (−1)ᵏ x²ᵏ / (2²ᵏ (k!)²): its odd coefficients are zero and aₙ = −aₙ₋₂/n² for n ≥ 2.
